title: Rockenfeller wins the first DTM race in Russia
dek: Mike Rockenfeller won the first DTM race in Russia from pole by 1.303 seconds from Audi stablemate Mattias Ekström, while Bruno Spengler's early contact with Miguel Molina left him 19th and 27 points adrift.

chapters.title: A new track and a title fight reopened
text: The DTM's sixth race of 2013, on Sunday 4 August, was the first in the series' history to be run in Russia. Moscow Raceway, a 2.555-kilometre circuit about 80 kilometres north-west of the capital, was designed by Hermann Tilke and had opened in 2012. No DTM driver had raced there, and teams had only one practice session on Saturday morning to find a set-up for a 74-lap race.

The championship arrived there in an unusual state. At the Norisring three weeks earlier Mattias Ekström had crossed the line first, but he was excluded for a parc fermé breach, and on 30 July the DMSB appeal court upheld that decision without moving anyone up, leaving the race without a winner. Mike Rockenfeller had meanwhile come from 21st on the grid to finish fifth in Nuremberg, and he took the lead of the standings with 69 points, two clear of Bruno Spengler on 67. Christian Vietoris was third on 55, Gary Paffett fourth on 47 and Robert Wickens fifth on 45.

Audi arrived with the championship leader in its ranks, but all three manufacturers were heading into unknown territory, since nobody had experience of the set-up or strategy needed on the third-shortest circuit of the 2013 calendar. A crowd of 45,000 was reported at the circuit over the weekend.

chapters.title: Pole decided by a presidential flight
text: Qualifying finished in unusual circumstances. Rockenfeller had set the pace in the third part of the session with a 58.423, and the final single-lap shoot-out was to feature him, Ekström, Augusto Farfus and Spengler. Shortly before it was due to start, the airspace above the circuit was closed because of the imminent flight of the Russian president's jet. That meant the circuit's medical helicopter could not take off, and with a closure of two hours announced, officials cancelled the last segment and set the front of the grid on the third-segment times.

Rockenfeller therefore took his second pole of the season, 0.181 seconds ahead of Ekström, with Farfus 0.254 off and Spengler 0.275 away on the second row. Jamie Green was fifth, Werner sixth and Paffett seventh as the best-placed Mercedes ahead of Pascal Wehrlein, Daniel Juncadella and Vietoris.

The unfamiliar track caught out several regulars. Wickens, the Norisring pole-sitter, was eliminated in the first segment and lined up 18th. Timo Glock was 17th, Martin Tomczyk 19th, Marco Wittmann 20th and Andy Priaulx 21st. Roberto Merhi spun and clipped a barrier in the closing minutes, ending up last on the grid in 22nd place.

chapters.title: Spengler hit, Mortara damaged
text: Rockenfeller and Ekström set the pace from the start, with Ekström on the harder standard tyres holding off Farfus, who had started on options. The first laps were crowded and cost several contenders. Early in the race Miguel Molina made contact with Spengler going into the first corner, spinning the title defender and damaging the rear of his BMW. Molina retired after five laps, while Spengler dropped to the back of the field.

Edoardo Mortara was another victim of the opening-lap melee. His Audi was hit by a rival and damaged, and he parked it in the pits after 31 laps. Juncadella was also involved in early contact, but kept going and was classified 18th, a lap down.

chapters.title: Option tyres decide the order
text: Strategy shaped the race, with two mandatory stops and a choice of option and standard tyres. Rockenfeller started on options and led until his first stop after a stint of around 45 laps. Ekström made an early first stop and spent a large part of the race at the front, so that the two Audis swapped the net lead around the pit-stop windows. Once the stops were over, Rockenfeller was back ahead, and he stayed there to the flag.

Adrien Tambay made the longest first stint of anyone, running more than 55 laps on a single set of options and enjoying clear air for much of the race. He started 12th, set the fastest lap on lap 70 and was fighting for the podium until the end. Paffett, meanwhile, spent most of the race in a battle with Green for fifth place.

chapters.title: Audi one-two, Farfus holds off Tambay
text: Rockenfeller crossed the line 1.303 seconds ahead of Ekström to win the first DTM race in Russia, with the pair more than ten seconds clear of the rest. Farfus took the last podium place for BMW, 11.393 seconds behind the winner, and in the closing laps he had to defend against the attacks of Tambay, finishing just 0.882 seconds ahead.

Paffett passed Green with about six laps to go to take fifth, leaving Green sixth. Joey Hand came through from 15th on the grid to seventh, ahead of Werner, Timo Scheider and Vietoris, who completed the top ten. Spengler, nursing his damaged car, was classified 19th and a lap down.

chapters.title: Rockenfeller opens up a 27-point lead
text: Audi called it a historic one-two, with five of its cars in the points and all four Abt Sportsline cars among them. Rockenfeller said the race matched his Brands Hatch win, starting from pole and finishing first, and that the key was winning qualifying and two clean pit stops from the Phoenix crew. He admitted that he had been too slow at the Norisring but said everything fitted together in Russia. Ekström said his car had been a dream to drive for the whole race. Dieter Gass, Audi's head of DTM, called the day an absolute dream, praised Rockenfeller's tyre management and said Ekström had shown what he could do after the Norisring disappointment. Wolfgang Ullrich, head of Audi Motorsport, pointed out that Russia was an important growth market for the brand.

The result reshaped the championship. Rockenfeller now had 94 points, 27 clear of Spengler on 67, with Paffett third on 57, Vietoris fourth on 56, Farfus fifth on 48 and Wickens sixth on 45. Spengler, who had finished with no points, said afterwards that his car had been practically undriveable after the contact, while his team boss Charly Lamm said the damage to the rear suspension left him fighting with blunt weapons.

For BMW, Farfus's third place was the only podium, with Hand and Werner the only other BMW drivers in the points. Farfus said it felt almost like a win. Mercedes had a flat day: Paffett's fifth was its best result, and he said the car lacked pace all weekend, but he was pleased to move to third in the standings. Tambay, who started 12th, finished fourth for his best result of the season so far.
The DTM moved on to the Nürburgring on 18 August, the seventh of the ten races of the season, where Rockenfeller's Phoenix team was to race at home.

facts.v: The final qualifying segment was cancelled when airspace over the circuit was closed for the president's flight, so the grid's front rows were set on Q3 times.
